title: No Verified Incident: Dog-Trade Claims Need Proof and Abolition
excerpt: No police record, court judgment, seizure, or health alert is supplied here. Public safety still demands verified evidence, quarantine, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A stolen companion animal leaves family loss behind. But no verified police seizure, court conviction, intercepted shipment, cyanide-bait incident, or named health alert accompanies this report. Publishing those claims as fact would replace evidence with invention. That gap matters: public anger must target documented theft, illegal transport, and regulatory failure—not unnamed communities.

Tradition cannot replace records

Claims about tradition, farm-raised dogs, or safe supply require proof: animal origin records, vaccination records, transport permits, quarantine compliance, inspection results, and traceable slaughterhouse documentation. None appears here. That does not prove every animal in trade was stolen or every shipment uninspected. It proves those claims remain unverified and cannot justify public confidence.

Biosecurity has no room for guesswork

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. WHO guidance supports immediate care.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply-chain failures are parallel biosecurity concerns, not automatically one causal chain. Officials must publish verifiable records. Communities deserve protection from stolen pets, illegal transport, uninspected slaughter, and disease risk.

Proof must lead reform

Vietnamese families, pet guardians, veterinarians, and local reformers can demand transparent enforcement without shaming a nation or its people. Public records should show what happened, where, when, and who acted. SDE’s campaign demand goes further than any single health target: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action—and follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.
